context: Force-directed network with 400 nodes across 7 labeled clusters (~600 edges, 80% intra-cluster), rendered on canvas with hover-based ego-network highlighting and a Tol bright colorblind-safe palette on a dark background.
first_impression: Seven distinct color clusters self-organize into clearly separated spatial blobs, making cluster structure immediately readable despite the large node count.
what_works: Low-opacity edges (0.15 alpha) prevent spaghetti despite 600 links, and the Tol bright 7-color palette produces perceptually distinct, well-separated hues that survive the dark background. Cluster-pull forces keep groups cohesive so structure is legible at a glance without hovering.
what_doesnt: At 400 nodes the individual marks are small enough that intra-cluster topology (hubs, bridges) is invisible without hover interaction, which cannot be assessed from a static screenshot. Drag reheats the simulation with alphaTarget(0.3), which on a large graph produces prolonged global churn that may disorient the viewer — staged settling would be less disruptive.
